findings.title: Accountability and Control Were Not Sufficient For Receipts at Two Locations Reviewed
findings.description: CCU had not established adequate accountability and control over cash receipts received at headquarters and one satellite office. Employees could alter critical data, mail receipts were not recorded immediately, and supervisory duties lacked independent review.

dollar_amounts.context: cash and checks received at two locations during fiscal year 2008
receipts in form of cash at CCU headquarters
receipts in form of checks at one satellite office

findings.recommendation: a. employees who have access to cash receipts not have the capability to adjust critical data on the automated accounts receivable system, b. CCU establish accountability over mail receipts by recording such payments immediately upon receipt and by documenting the transfer of funds to the cash office, c. CCU establish adequate procedures and controls at the aforementioned satellite office to ensure all receipts are properly controlled.

findings.title: CCU Lacked Procedures to Ensure That All Deposit Adjustments Were Identified and Properly Investigated
findings.description: CCU lacked procedures to ensure all deposit adjustments were identified and properly investigated. Test of 25 bank adjustments disclosed that for six adjustments totaling $20,000, CCU could not document investigation. Bank adjustments totaled approximately $477,000 during fiscal year 2007.

dollar_amounts.context: adjustments totaling where CCU could not document investigation
bank adjustments total during fiscal year 2007

findings.recommendation: a. use the adjustment reports received from the STO to identify all deposit adjustments, b. properly investigate and resolve the deposit adjustments and that documentation of such efforts be maintained (repeat).

findings.title: Certain Debt Collection Tools, Such as Wage Garnishments, Were Not Pursued in a Timely Manner
findings.description: CCU did not always pursue wage garnishments when eligible wages were identified. Test of 10 debtors with accounts totaling $362,000 disclosed that for 8 debtors owing approximately $162,000, CCU had not initiated wage garnishments as early as February 2006. Property lien matches were not analyzed timely (last match Dec 2005).

dollar_amounts.context: aggregate debt totaling who had wages that could possibly be subject to garnishment
accounts totaling in test of wage garnishments
owed by 8 debtors where CCU had not initiated wage garnishments

findings.recommendation: a. CCU ensure that timely follow-up collection efforts are made with regard to wage garnishments (repeat), b. property lien matches be performed on a regular basis (at least semiannually) and that the results be pursued on a timely basis (repeat), c. all debt collection efforts be documented (repeat).

findings.title: CCU Did Not Conduct Comprehensive Collection Actions on 22,000 Delinquent Accounts Totaling $60 Million
findings.description: CCU did not conduct all possible collection actions on 22,000 delinquent accounts totaling $60 million as of March 12, 2008. A vacancy in the collector position responsible for cases between $2,000 and $10,000 resulted in cases not actively pursued.

dollar_amounts.context: delinquent accounts totaling where CCU did not conduct comprehensive collection actions

findings.recommendation: We recommend that CCU ensure that all significant cases are subject to comprehensive collection actions.

findings.title: CCU Did Not Adequately Pursue Collection on Certain Delinquent Uninsured Motorist Penalties Accounts
findings.description: Test of 10 delinquent installment plans with principal balances totaling $82,086 disclosed that for 7 plans totaling $52,604, CCU did not notify MVA of collection lapse. No referrals were made to PCA for insurance lapse fines due to logistical problems.

dollar_amounts.context: principal balances totaling in test of delinquent installment plans
principal balances totaling where CCU did not notify MVA

findings.recommendation: a. provide timely notification to the MVA of delinquent installment plans, b. implement an appropriate process to forward delinquent insurance lapse fines and penalties to the PCA.

findings.title: CCU Needs to Work With the Motor Vehicle Administration to Address the Timely Collection of Delinquent Uninsured Motorist Penalties
findings.description: Policy Issue. Significant delays (up to two years) could occur before accounts are forwarded to CCU due to MVA procedure waiting for event occurrence. CCU management stated it could not deviate from policy requiring total amount due.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that CCU work in conjunction with MVA to develop a better method of assessing and collecting uninsured motorist penalties. For example, CCU should consider the feasibility of having uninsured motorist accounts transferred to CCU on an interim basis so that the accounts could be certified for the State’s tax refund intercept program.

findings.title: CCU Did Not Ensure the Validity of Signatures Authorizing Account Adjustments Received From State Agencies
findings.description: Test of 15 adjustments totaling $485,000 disclosed that for five adjustments totaling approximately $197,000 authorizing signatures did not match. One adjustment eliminating a $39,000 receivable was processed in error. Approximately 31,000 adjustment forms totaling approximately $27 million were received in fiscal year 2007.

dollar_amounts.context: adjustments totaling where signatures did not match
receivable eliminated in adjustment processed in error
adjustment forms received in fiscal year 2007

findings.recommendation: We recommend that CCU develop procedures for ensuring that account adjustment request forms are signed by an authorized agency employee.

findings.title: Critical Capabilities on the Automated Accounts Receivable System Were Not Adequately Controlled or Subject to Independent Approvals
findings.description: 60 individuals could change desk codes without independent approval. All individuals with access could change account status codes without independent approval. Improper changes could result in accounts not being actively worked.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that CCU establish adequate controls over all critical transactions. Specifically, we recommend that access to critical transactions should be a. limited to individuals who require such access for their job duties, and b. subject to independent approval.

findings.title: CCU Did Not Adequately Monitor the Private Collection Agency It Used
findings.description: CCU did not conduct documented inspections of PCA during audit period. Approximately 19,000 cases met criteria for return but had not been returned. CCU lacked assurance that PCA had adequate procedures (did not obtain reports for FY2005 and 2007). During fiscal years 2006 through 2008, CCU referred approximately 161,000 debts totaling $166 million to the PCA.

dollar_amounts.context: cases that met contract's criteria for return but had not been returned
debts totaling referred to the PCA during fiscal years 2006 through 2008
commissions paid to the PCA during fiscal year 2008

findings.recommendation: a. that referred accounts are subject to all appropriate and required collection practices... (repeat), b. that all uncollected accounts are returned from the contractor when required; c. that the PCA has adequate procedures to safeguard collections of State funds and sensitive client information by obtaining and reviewing copies of the PCA’s audited financial statements and management letters.

findings.title: CCU Did Not Adequately Address Backup and Transfer of Critical Data
findings.description: CCU stored backup tapes in same room as servers. Tapes not encrypted. Sensitive information sent via USPS not encrypted. Best practices specify encryption for confidentiality/sensitivity.
findings.recommendation: a. the weekly backups of RCS servers be maintained at a secure offsite location, and b. CCU encrypt backup data sent to offsite storage and to other State agencies.

extraction.agency_response_summary: The Department of Budget and Management agreed with all recommendations. They noted that personnel changes were made, systems are being updated or implemented (e.g., new collection system in FY2011), processes for monitoring and documentation have been improved, and specific actions like offsite storage and encryption were completed by late 2008/early 2009.
extraction.extraction_notes: Report date taken from transmittal letter. Audit period from scope section. Repeat findings identified via asterisks in TOC and 'repeat' markers in recommendations. Dollar amounts converted to integers.
